name: Solacin
description: Solacin is a mild anxiolytic and prosocial compound that reduces social anxiety and inhibition without the cognitive impairment of alcohol, replacing social fear with a warm, genuine interest in the people around you. It's the clean, functional social drug of 2200 — you're still yourself, still sharp, still in control, just no longer afraid. Novafold markets it as 'connection support' and it's available over the counter in most Tier 2-4 pharmacies.
effects: Elimination of social anxiety and self-consciousness
Genuine interest in and warmth toward people around you
Enhanced sense of belonging and social comfort
side_effects: Overcandor — users may disclose more than intended
Post-use social anxiety spike as brain recalibrates ('the rebounce')
Long-term use associated with atrophied natural social skills
Rare: allergic reaction in users with certain geneware modifications
cultural_context: Solacin is so normalized in GLMZ that many people don't think of it as a drug — it's what you take before a work function, a first date, a difficult conversation, a party where you don't know anyone. In Tier 2, it's cheaper than alcohol and has no hangover. In Tier 3, the Novafold branded version (in its distinctive pale blue capsule) is practically a social prop — being seen to take Solacin signals that you're a functional, socially responsible adult. The 'rebounce' — the post-use anxiety spike — is the drug's most discussed cultural feature, and has given rise to the practice of 'stacking' doses to avoid it.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 corporate HR department has been quietly adding Solacin to the water dispensers on meeting floors — productivity and 'team cohesion scores' have improved dramatically, and someone has just noticed the pharmacy receipts

A character with social anxiety has been on daily Solacin for three years and has never developed the social skills the drug was supposed to supplement — now there's a shortage, and they have to navigate a critical situation completely sober for the first time in their adult life

The 'overcandor' effect has been weaponized — someone has developed a high-dose Solacin variant used in interrogation, not as a truth serum exactly, but as a compound that makes people genuinely want to share everything they know
